I wrote 5 review comments to `bench/runs/calcom_cal.com-14943/vanilla/comments.json`. All of them are on `packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts`, and they come from reading the code only; nothing was run.

1. **The cleanup deletes more than SMS reminders (line 38).** The new `retryCount > 1` branch of the delete filter doesn't check the method. So this SMS cron deletes any reminder with `retryCount > 1`, including email or WhatsApp ones, as soon as anything else starts using the new column.
2. **Locked accounts lose their reminders (line 178).** `scheduleSMS` returns `undefined` when a user or team is locked for SMS sending. The PR counts that as a failed attempt, so after two cron runs those reminders are deleted and don't come back when the lock is lifted.
3. **Temporary errors cause permanent deletion (line 190).** Every exception counts as a retry: hitting the monthly rate limit, a Twilio outage or network error, and errors from building the message. The PR is meant to stop retrying invalid numbers, but as written a short outage also deletes valid reminders.
4. **One failed update stops the whole run (line 190).** The retry-count update inside the `catch` isn't protected. If it throws, for example because the reminder was deleted at the same moment, the loop ends and the remaining reminders aren't processed.
5. **Duplicate SMS and texts that can't be cancelled (line 195).** If Twilio accepts the message but saving `scheduled: true` and the Twilio ID fails, this is counted as a failure. The next run sends a duplicate, and once the row is deleted, cancelling the booking can't cancel the queued texts. I also suggested `{ increment: 1 }` instead of `reminder.retryCount + 1`, so an out-of-date read can't overwrite another update.
